title: Find files and justify filesystem placement
goal: Use bounded name/type/size/time searches and explain configuration, logs and local data placement.
challenge: In the model tree locate the current log, old log and configuration by verified predicates. Record sizes/time criteria and explain where configuration, changing logs and local static data belong on real Linux. Do not modify actual system paths.

steps.command: w=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/local-search.XXXXXX") && cd "$w" && pwd && here() { case "$w" in "$HOME"/local-search.??????) ;; *) return 19;; esac; test "${w%/*}" = "$HOME" && test -d "$w" && test ! -L "$w" && test "$(realpath -e "$w")" = "$w" && test "$(stat -c %U:%a "$w")" = learner:700 && test "$(pwd -P)" = "$w"; }; fresh() { for f; do test ! -e "$f" && test ! -L "$f" || return 19; done; }; here
steps.explanation: Create a unique learner-owned guest workspace; stop on error and record its absolute path. Reopening boots the disk, not these shell variables. Never use the host terminal.
steps.expected: A new private directory; no pre-existing files are changed.

steps.command:
here && fresh etc var usr placement.txt && { mkdir etc var usr; mkdir var/log usr/local; mkdir usr/local/share; printf 'setting=on
' > etc/app.conf; printf 'current observation
' > var/log/current.log; printf 'old
' > var/log/old.log; touch -d '3 days ago' var/log/old.log; printf 'reference
' > usr/local/share/readme.txt; }
steps.explanation: This is a small model tree inside your home, not the real root filesystem. touch changes only a fixture timestamp, never the clock.
steps.expected: Separate configuration, variable logs and local static data.

steps.explanation: Quote the glob so find receives it. c means bytes; other size units have rounding. -P does not follow symbolic links.
steps.expected: Two logs; configuration/current log satisfy the byte-size condition.

steps.command: here && { find -P var/log -maxdepth 1 -type f -mtime +1 -print; find -P var/log -maxdepth 1 -type f -mmin -5 -print; }
steps.explanation: mtime counts whole 24-hour periods; +1 selects more than one completed period. mmin uses minutes. Read/retain timestamps and avoid assuming exact age from a filename.
steps.expected: old.log versus recently created current.log; may need to recreate only this fixture after a long pause.

steps.command: here && { stat -c '%n %s %y' etc/app.conf var/log/current.log var/log/old.log usr/local/share/readme.txt; printf '%s\n' 'CONFIG etc/app.conf' 'VARIABLE var/log/current.log' 'STATIC usr/local/share/readme.txt' > placement.txt; cat placement.txt; }
steps.explanation: Explain /etc, /var/log and /usr/local/share roles. This narrow model does not cover the entire FHS or locate/updatedb databases.
steps.expected: Evidence and placement rationale; no real system change.

hints: Record units, not just a number.
Use explicit root and maxdepth; do not search the whole disk.
review: I retained actual output and checked the required contents, metadata or identity, not just command success.
I can explain the stated limitations, demonstrate the incorrect case, preserve originals and clean up only my recorded workspace.
coverage: LPIC-1 v5.0 partial 103.3 /104.7. Self-reviewed and unscored: the application does not inspect guest results. No full-objective or exam-readiness claim.
